title: Open interest, rollover and market indicators
objectives: Read open interest, volume and the put-call ratio.
body_md:
## Open interest and volume

- **Volume** is contracts traded in a period. **Open interest (OI)** is contracts still open (not squared off).
- Rising price with rising OI usually means **fresh long buying**; rising price with falling OI hints at **short covering**.
- Falling price with rising OI suggests **fresh shorts**.

## Put-call ratio (PCR)

**PCR = put open interest (or volume) ÷ call open interest (or volume).** High PCR can show hedging or bearishness; extreme readings are sometimes read as contrarian signals. It is an input, not a forecast.

## Rollover

Before expiry, traders **roll** by closing the near-month and opening the next. High rollover with rising OI shows continued conviction; the **roll cost** is the spread between the two months.

## Arbitrage signals

A gap between futures and fair value (cost of carry) invites cash-and-carry arbitrage, which pulls prices back.

| Indicator | Reading |
|---|---|
| Price up, OI up | Strong trend, fresh longs |
| Price up, OI down | Short covering |
| Price down, OI up | Fresh shorts |
| Price down, OI down | Long unwinding |

> **Exam tip:** Memorise the four price-OI combinations.
example: A stock rises 3% while OI jumps 15%. New longs are entering, which supports the move more than short covering would.
say: Open interest shows how many contracts remain open, not who is right.
PCR is one input among several.
never: High volume and open interest are the same thing.

check.why: New money is entering on the long side.
